did_you_know.text: The word matzevah usually refers to an upright stone set up as a memorial or marker. Here, the twelve stones represent the twelve tribes of Israel.
In the phrase “We will do and we will hear,” the word “hear” can also mean “heed” or “obey.” The phrase therefore emphasizes both action and attentive listening.

The biblical word sappir does not necessarily mean the modern gemstone sapphire; it may refer to the blue stone now called lapis lazuli. That is why translations differ in how they identify the stone.
In the ancient world, sharing food and drink often marked friendship, peace, or a covenant. The meal described here therefore gives the event a sense of closeness and celebration.
Hur is not merely a minor figure: later, during the battle with Amalek, he helps Aaron support Moses’ hands. The Bible thus presents him as a trusted leader.

The number forty also appears in other extended biblical periods, such as the forty days of the Flood and the forty days the spies explored the land. It often marks a long period of transition, preparation, or testing.
